analyst_view.overall: Early view: The Nordderby comes with Bremen sixth after their best start since 2018/19 under Daniel Thioune, built on Niclas Füllkrug's league-leading nine goals and a habit of scoring late. Hamburg beat ten-man Gladbach 3-1 to end three straight competitive defeats, but have lost four of five away games and Merlin Polzin's squad is thin; one injury tracker lists Miro Muheim, scorer of three long-range goals, out until late November.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. Hamburg's poor away record and 20 goals conceded point up, but derbies are often cagey and Bremen were held scoreless at Stuttgart despite 13 shots. I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 9.4 corners, 5.6 for Bremen. I lean slightly higher: 14 of Bremen's 17 goals have come after half-time and they push hard late on, which tends to produce a run of corners, while Hamburg defending a lead or a draw will clear wide.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards, already high because of the derby. Bremen took three yellows in each of their last two games and Hamburg four at Frankfurt, which supports a busy afternoon for the referee, but the number already reflects that, so I stay level.

shots.text: The site has 31.2 shots, 19.6 for Bremen. Bremen took 13 at Stuttgart and their attack runs mostly through Füllkrug, so nearly 20 at home looks high, even against a side that has lost four of five away. I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 on target. In line with fewer shots I lean slightly lower, although Hamburg's long-range shooters (Muheim if fit, and Albert Grønbæk, who scored from distance against Gladbach) can test the keeper from anywhere.
